title: Itsekiri people
comment:
The original Pasquier citation must be removed entirely. It concerns French missionary priests in nineteenth-century Kentucky and has nothing to do with the Itsekiri or Nigeria.

The statements about a “complex genetic mix,” “racial groups,” and the Itsekiri supposedly being the only almost completely heterogeneous southern Nigerian population are not supported by genetic research. 

To summarize all changes: Rewrote the section using reliable academic sources; corrected the linguistic classi...

title: Itsekiri people
comment:
/* Origins and ethnogenesis */ I removed the Umale/Egungun passage because the cited material does not support the claim that the pre-Ginuwa Yoruba-speaking settlers were collectively called Umale or Egungun. Moore actually records a different tradition in which umale were immortal or supernatural beings living among Ijaw, Urhobo and Mahin inhabitants. That is religious or legendary material, not evidence identifying an historical Yoruba population. 

The Roth, parliamentary and Gallwey block...

title: Itsekiri people
comment:
/* Formation of the Warri Kingdom */ I correct the original implication that Ginuwa personally established the capital at Okotomu. In Lloyd’s account, Ginuwa died at Ijala and the capital was established by his son Ijijen. It also properly presents the Okere account as a tradition about remnants of a Benin force; Lloyd does not say that they joined an “aboriginal Yoruba group.” 

It also corrects the claim that the monarchy continued uninterrupted to the present: Olu Akengbuwa’s death in 1848...

comment: /* Group identity */ Corrected the linguistic classification and geographic scope. Yoruboid and Edekiri are language groupings, not one mutually intelligible ***dialect continuum***.
